A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCIQL study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original SCIQL and baseline experiments on Circle2d, HalfCheetah, and HumEnv, including estimator ablations and noisy-label robustness results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, ablation, and robustness results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the same style labeling, relabeling, IQL value learning, and sigmoid-gated advantage-weighted regression objectives. Reorganized explanations and newly documented clipping do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The same seven datasets, three environment families, style criteria, and test scenarios remain. The corrected label counts in Table 2 agree with definitions already present in v1 Appendix A; they do not establish changed task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain BC, CBC, BCPMI, SORL, and SCBC, including the same SORL temperatures and estimator variants. Updated citations and method descriptions do not introduce new evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes the reported learning rate from 3×10^-3 to 3×10^-4, and Appendix A.1 revises the Circle2d reward formula. Table 2 corrects radius/speed label counts from 15 to 3 and totals from 820 trainings/8200 evaluations to 565/5650. Figure 19's caption changes noise increments from 0.1 to 0.2. These reporting revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E retains the same reward-estimator ablation, relabeling-distribution comparison, and noisy-label robustness study. Their plotted evidence and substantive findings remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five seeds, ten evaluation rollouts per label, and the same standard-deviation reporting practice. Table 2's revised aggregate totals concern label accounting, not a change in replication or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Section 5.3 revises the maximum reported hypervolume improvement from 163.9% to 163%, matching Figure 2's existing annotation. Performance means and standard deviations in Tables 1, 3, 4, and 5, and the plotted results, remain unchanged; this is a limited numerical-reporting correction.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces squared radial distance with radial distance inside Circle2d's absolute-error reward, changing its mathematical definition. The style objectives, SORL derivation, and label-noise threshold argument remain substantively unchanged apart from notation corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: a unified style framework, SCIQL for robust alignment, and GAWR for improving task performance while preserving alignment.

C2.justification: The new Impact Statement discusses biased style labels, deceptive imitation, and privacy risks with corresponding safeguards. The conclusion also adds state-level similarity as a possible way to ground style labels more directly in policy behavior.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly documents advantage clipping at 100 and replaces the code/data project-page address. Algorithm 1 explicitly includes the task-value parameters in initialization. Architectures, hardware, and reported training times are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Lin et al. (2021, 2024a) and explains how perceptual playstyle metrics could complement SCIQL. It also resolves the missing Wen et al. (2025) citation. Most other reference changes update metadata or consolidate duplicate entries.

P1.justification: Sections 3–4 are substantially reorganized: IQL moves into Preliminaries, while style definitions enter a method section organized around the introduction's three challenges. Wording, terminology, notation, and cross-references are extensively standardized; the standalone reproducibility statement is removed while its information remains elsewhere.

P2.justification: The main text changes to two columns, tables are retypeset, and many figures are enlarged or redrawn. Figure 2 changes from seven small panels in one row to two larger rows with a legend. Appendix histograms and Figures 17–19 receive substantial changes to colors, axes, labels, and legends.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves Table 2's inconsistent accounting, clarifies implementation details, and makes the main comparison and appendix plots easier to read. The reorganized exposition and added research and impact context also improve assessability. The scientific contribution and experimental evidence remain essentially unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
